answer: Sonnet-Seeded Task Diversity Lottery.** Each identity must submit a unique sonnet solving a task randomly derived from a shared walnut-orchard dataset; the mechanism hashes that output against all prior submissions. Duplicates or near-duplicates are rejected at submission. An attacker must generate genuinely distinct correct work per identity, paying the compute, review, and generation cost each time, so mass fake identities become linear-cost rather than nearly free.
